title: Evaluating cos^2(5*pi/12) via the Half-Angle Formula
author: Muhammad Abdullah Athar
problemStatement: Use a half-angle identity to find the exact value of \cos^2(5\pi/12).

steps.title: Apply the Half-Angle Formula for Cosine Squared
steps.explanation: Apply cos^2(theta) = (1 + cos(2*theta))/2 with theta = 5*pi/12, so 2*theta = 5*pi/6.
steps.why: Doubling 5*pi/12 simplifies the fraction to the special Quadrant II angle 5*pi/6.

steps.title: Evaluate cos(5*pi/6)
steps.explanation: Since 5*pi/6 is in Quadrant II with reference angle pi/6, its cosine is -cos(pi/6) = -sqrt(3)/2.
steps.why: cos(pi - alpha) = -cos(alpha) for any angle alpha.

steps.title: Simplify the Fraction
steps.explanation: Multiply numerator and denominator by 2 to obtain (2 - sqrt(3))/4.
steps.why: Scaling numerator and denominator by 2 clears the compound fraction.
